answer.exemplar: Real power is apparent power times power factor, so lower power factor means less real power for the same apparent power.

questions.explanation: P = S*cos(phi). Lower pf reduces real power. The tempting wrong idea is that apparent power is all real power.
questions.hint: Real power equals apparent times pf.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Reactive power of a lagging load
questions.stem: In an architect's brief, V = 480 V, I = 10 A, pf = 0.8 lagging; find reactive power in VAR.
questions.explanation: Q = 480*10*0.6 = 2880 VAR. Using cos gives 3840 W real power.
questions.hint: Use sin of the phase angle.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_EM
questions.topic: Apparent power from the power triangle
questions.stem: An architect's brief gives P = 2000 W and Q = 1500 VAR; find apparent power in VA.
questions.explanation: S = sqrt(2000^2 + 1500^2) = 2500 VA. Linear sum 3500 is wrong.
questions.hint: Use Pythagorean sum of P and Q.
